description: Insurance-sector control schema for the CoSAI AI Shared Responsibility Framework. Maps SRF layers and accountable personas to NAIC Model Bulletin AIS Program requirements, NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool dimensions, Colorado Regulation 10-1-1 (3 CCR 702-10), NYDFS Circular Letter No. 7, EU AI Act articles, and OWASP LLM Top 10.
regulatory_context: The NAIC Model Bulletin on the Use of AI Systems (December 2023) requires a written AIS Program covering governance, risk management, internal controls, and third-party AI oversight but prescribes no control catalog. Colorado Regulation 10-1-1 (amended effective October 15, 2025) extends ECDIS governance to private passenger auto and health benefit insurers, with governance frameworks due on request from July 1, 2026. The NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool multistate pilot (January to September 2026, twelve states) gives examiners a standardized review framework for market conduct exams. This schema operationalizes those requirements with named accountable personas, measurable thresholds, and machine-readable evidence.
mapping_status_note: NAIC Model Bulletin, NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool, Colorado Regulation 10-1-1, NYDFS Circular Letter No. 7, EU AI Act, and OWASP LLM Top 10 mappings verified against primary sources 2026-07-05 (adopted bulletin text; DRAFT AI Systems Evaluation Tool 4.0 pilot draft, pre-adoption; Amended Regulation 10-1-1 effective Oct 15, 2025; Circular Letter No. 7 final text; Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 final numbering, correcting Article 28 (Notifying Authorities, unrelated) to Article 25/26 for third-party and deployer citations; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 edition, correcting the pre-2025 LLM numbering used in the original hints). The NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool remains an unadopted pilot draft as of July 2026 (adoption anticipated NAIC Fall National Meeting 2026); its exhibit/ref citations should be re-verified on adoption. Do not substitute invented IDs. CIS Controls v8.1 mappings added 2026-07-12 as part of the AI security lifecycle plan, verified against the official CIS Controls v8 list (18 controls, 153 safeguards; cisecurity.org) and the CIS Controls v8.1 AI and Large Language Models Companion Guide (published April 20, 2026). Mapped at the control level, not the individual safeguard level, since the Companion Guide interprets safeguards through an AI-aware lens rather than reassigning safeguard numbers. Applied only where a defensible correspondence exists; most controls in this schema have no CIS nexus and carry no cis key. NIST AI RMF 1.0 subcategory mappings added 2026-07-28. The AI RMF is the horizontal US risk framework both the model-risk and market-conduct supervisors point to, so every control carries a subcategory. CSA AI Controls Matrix v1.0.3 mappings added 2026-07-28. Applied only where a control objective genuinely corresponds; controls with no AICM nexus carry no aicm key. Objective IDs and titles are reused from the set already verified in the finance schema so no ID is invented.
eu_ai_act_citation_format: EU AI Act citations use the form 'Article N' (spelled out, sub-provisions as 'Article 10(2)(f)') and 'Annex X', an optional short gloss in parentheses, multiple citations separated by '; '. 'TBD:' prefix marks an unverified mapping; 'N/A' means no EU AI Act nexus. Do not substitute invented article numbers.
naic_model_bulletin_citation_format: NAIC Model Bulletin citations use the form 'Section N, Guideline X.y (topic gloss)' for content inside the Section 3 AIS Program Guidelines (numbered 1.0-4.0 with lettered sub-items, independent of the outer Section 1-4 numbering), 'Section N, Item X.y' for the Section 4 examination-request list, or 'Section N (background text)' for legislative-authority or introductory citations; multiple citations separated by '; '. Verified against the adopted bulletin text (Dec 4, 2023, content.naic.org) in July 2026. The bulletin does not define or use the term ECDIS and does not address platform or infrastructure cybersecurity (encryption, access control, egress, interface security testing, CVE disclosure) or adverse-action reason codes; 'N/A' marks those confirmed no-nexus controls.
naic_eval_tool_citation_format: NAIC AI Systems Evaluation Tool citations use the form 'Exhibit {A|B (Narrative)|B (Checklist)|C|D}, Ref/Q N' referencing the DRAFT AI Systems Evaluation Tool 4.0 (Clean), posted for public comment at content.naic.org (12-state pilot March-September 2026; adoption anticipated at the NAIC Fall National Meeting 2026). The Tool is unadopted as of July 2026: citations bind to this draft's exhibit and reference numbering, which may shift on adoption and should be re-verified at that time. Multiple citations separated by '; '. 'N/A' means no exhibit field addresses the control's subject.
co_reg_10_1_1_citation_format: Colorado citations use the form 'Section N(X)(y)' referencing Amended Regulation 10-1-1 (3 CCR 702-10), effective October 15, 2025. Verified against the amended regulation text in July 2026. Scope note: Section 5's governance and quantitative-testing requirements apply only to individually issued life, private passenger auto, and health benefit plan insurers, the unfair-discrimination testing duty in Section 5(A)(11) is scoped to race, and Section 5(A)(5)'s human-responsibility provision applies only to health benefit plan insurers. The regulation does not address platform or infrastructure cybersecurity (encryption, access control, egress, interface security testing); 'N/A' marks those confirmed no-nexus controls.
nydfs_cl7_citation_format: NYDFS CL 7 citations use the form 'Section N.X, paragraph(s) NN' referencing Insurance Circular Letter No. 7 (2024), issued July 11, 2024 (I. Purpose and Background, paras 1-9; II. Fairness Principles, paras 10-19, subsections A Data Actuarial Validity, B Unfair and Unlawful Discrimination, C Analyzing for Unfair or Unlawful Discrimination; III. Governance and Risk Management, paras 20-37, subsections A Board and Senior Management Oversight, B Policies Procedures and Documentation, C Risk Management and Internal Controls, D Third-Party Vendors; IV. Transparency, paras 38-45, subsections E Disclosure and Notice, F Clarification of CL 1 (2019)). Verified against the circular letter text in July 2026. 'N/A' means the letter does not address the control's subject.
owasp_llm_citation_format: OWASP LLM Top 10 citations use the form 'LLMNN (Category Title)' referencing the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2025 edition (genai.owasp.org), which renumbered and reworked the 2023/2024 list: former LLM06 Sensitive Information Disclosure is now LLM02; former LLM09 Improper Output Handling is now LLM05; former LLM08 Excessive Agency is now LLM06; former LLM03 Training Data Poisoning is now split between LLM03 Supply Chain and LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning. Multiple citations separated by '; '. Verified against the 2025 edition in July 2026. 'N/A' means no category addresses the control's subject.

controls.title: AIS Program Document Currency and Board Approval
controls.description: The insurer must maintain a written AI Systems (AIS) Program approved by the board or a designated senior executive. The program must cover governance structure, risk management framework, internal controls, and third-party AI oversight. It must be reviewed and reapproved on the cadence defined in SRF-L1-MON-001 and be available to the regulator on request per CO Regulation 10-1-1.

Coverage is defined as the percentage of known production AI systems appearing in the inventory.

controls.title: Prompt Injection Defense for Consumer-Facing AI
controls.description: AI applications and agentic systems with consumer-facing interfaces in insurance workflows (chatbots, claims intake, policy service) must implement documented defenses against prompt injection attacks.
